title: Local exactness of a sectionwise Cech augmentation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U:I\to\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ any family of opens, $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf, $D$ a nonnegative cochain complex of module sheaves, and $\epsilon:F[0]\to D$ a chain map. Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $P(W)(V)=F(W\cap V)$ with restricted $A$-action, and $C^\bullet=\check C^\bullet(U,P)$, the full unnormalized Cech complex. Suppose given natural presheaf isomorphisms $e_p:\operatorname{forget}(D^p)\simeq C^p$ with $\operatorname{forget}(d_D^p)e_{p+1}=e_p d_C^p$ for every $p$. Suppose that on every open $V$, each coordinate of $e_0\epsilon^0$, indexed by $y:\operatorname{Fin}(1)\to I$, is the restriction $F(V)\to F((\prod_lU_{y(l)})\cap V)$. For every $i\in I$, restriction of $\epsilon$ to the open subscheme $U_i$ is a quasi-isomorphism. There is no covering assumption, no assertion of global exactness, and no assumption identifying the terms of $D$ with products of open direct images.

proof.text: Apply lem-pc-cech-local-augmentation-kernel to obtain the kernel universal property for the restricted degree-zero augmentation. A kernel inclusion is monic and its kernel short complex is exact. CochainComplex.quasiIsoAt₀_iff and ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_of_zeros therefore prove the restricted augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism in degree zero. Both differentials of the single source and the incoming differential of the nonnegative target vanish.

In degree p+1 the single source has a zero object. Restriction sends this zero object to zero, so ShortComplex.exact_of_isZero_X₂ proves source exactness without an exactness assumption on restriction. Apply lem-pc-cech-local-positive-exact for target exactness. Mathlib quasiIsoAt_iff_exactAt yields the quasi-isomorphism in this degree.

Case-split every natural-number degree into zero or successor and assemble the degreewise conclusions using the constructor of QuasiIso. No change to the statement, the unit route, or the meaning of any definition is made.

CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor constructs a complex from an already given opposite-opens functor. It does not construct that module-sheaf functor, its section identifications or its augmentation.

Mathlib FormalCoproduct.extraDegeneracyCech provides an extra degeneracy of a simplicial formal coproduct with a chosen terminal section. It does not provide the cosimplicial module-sheaf comparison or the restricted augmentation. Searches of lean/Sheaf and lean/WeilConjectures found no existing declaration for either intermediate.

theorem augmented_cech_sheaf_quasiIso_restrict
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens) (F : X.Modules)
    (D : CochainComplex X.Modules ℕ)
    (ε : (CochainComplex.single₀ X.Modules).obj F ⟶ D)
    (e : ∀ p : ℕ, (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).obj
          (D.X p).val ≅
        ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj
          ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
            (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat)).X p)
    (hd : ∀ p : ℕ,
        (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
            (D.d p (p + 1)).val ≫ (e (p + 1)).hom =
          (e p).hom ≫ ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj
            ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
              (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat)).d p (p + 1))
    (hε : ∀ (y : Fin 1 → ι) (V : X.Opens),
        ((PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
            ((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 F).inv ≫ ε.f 0).val ≫
          (e 0).hom ≫
            Pi.π (fun y : Fin 1 → ι =>
              ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
                (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat).obj
                  (op (∏ᶜ fun l => U (y l)))) y).app (op V) =
          F.presheafModuleCat.map (prod.snd : (∏ᶜ fun l => U (y l)) ⨯ V ⟶ V).op) (i : ι) :
    QuasiIso (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map ε)
